lines.trans: Your soup, buddy, enjoy your meal.
Viktor Petrovich, what are you doing?
I am doing what I must do.
But an important critic is sitting right there!
I do not care who is sitting there.
This guest ordered soup earlier.
The critic is very angry, he will leave!
Let him leave if he does not know how to wait.
You are risking our restaurant's reputation.
Even if he were three times a critic!
I serve all guests in turn.
In my kitchen everyone is equal!

meanings.note: + 3rd person verb: 'пусть строят' = let them build

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'pleasant' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('!') (= Enjoy your meal!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Very well! Have a pleasant evening.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: to leave, to go away (on foot)
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ходить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to leave', forming an aspectual pair with 'уйти'.

examples.text: Уходи отсюда скорее, пока шеф не увидел тебя без формы!
examples.trans: Get out of here quickly before the chef sees you without a uniform!

meanings.note: стоять в очереди = to stand in a queue; без очереди = jumping the queue
Secondary conversational sense ('turn') (моя очередь = it's my turn) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'three times'.

examples.text: Да будь он хоть трижды критик!
examples.trans: Even if he were three times a critic!

examples.text: Да будь он хоть трижды знаменитый ресторанный критик!
examples.trans: Even if he were three times a famous restaurant critic!

examples.text: Шеф заставил Макса трижды переделать этот сложный соус.
examples.trans: The chef made Max remake this complex sauce three times.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('at least') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'earlier'.

examples.text: В моей комнате раньше дядя Миша жил.
examples.trans: Uncle Misha used to live in my room.
There used to be an old park here.

examples.text: Подождите. В моей комнате раньше дядя Миша жил.
examples.trans: Wait. Uncle Misha used to live in my room.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'soupe' in the Petrine era.

examples.text: Сегодня на кухне сварили вкусный суп.
examples.trans: Today in the kitchen they cooked delicious soup.
I like hot soup very much!

examples.text: Мы добавим таблетку в её суп?
examples.trans: Shall we add the pill into her soup?

meanings.note: 'а то' at the start of a sentence: 'а то мы уже начали беспокоиться' = we were starting to worry

examples.text: А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: We were starting to worry, you see.

examples.text: Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
злая собака = vicious dog; а почему вы такая злая? = why are you so hostile?
From French 'réputation' / Latin 'reputatio' (consideration, public standing).

examples.text: У меня репутация, я не проигрываю.
examples.trans: I have a reputation, I don't lose.

examples.text: У меня репутация, я не проигрываю. У твоего Самсонова шансов нет.
examples.trans: I have a reputation, I don't lose. Your Samsonov has no chance.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'идеть'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to sit', forming an aspectual pair with 'посидеть'.

examples.trans: Why are you sitting in the corner?

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'along' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('along, around') (+ dative) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('by (phone)') ('по телефону') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'авать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to serve'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to serve, hand') (food or items) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Как будто ты подаёшь на развод.
examples.trans: As if you are filing for divorce.

examples.text: Подавай мясо на горячей тарелке гостям.
examples.trans: Serve the meat to the guests on a hot plate.

examples.text: Вика, скорее подавай гостям горячие блюда!
examples.trans: Vika, serve the hot dishes to the guests quickly!

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Abstract masculine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'guest'.

examples.trans: All the guests love them very much.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером к нам придут гости.
examples.trans: Guests are coming to our place tonight.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
Secondary conversational sense ('it') (for masculine and neuter things) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to make') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: almost always in 'всё равно' = it doesn't matter; мне всё равно = I don't care

examples.text: Мне всё равно. Что ты, что он.
examples.trans: It's all the same to me. You or him.

уметь.gloss: to know how to, to be able to

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'меть'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know how to', forming an aspectual pair with 'суметь'.

examples.text: Эх, Паша, Паша. Ты считать не умеешь.
examples.trans: Oh, Pasha, Pasha. You can't count.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to order', paired with 'заказывать'.

examples.text: Если опоздают, пицца бесплатно. Может, закажем?
examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free. Maybe we should order?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to wait', forming an aspectual pair with 'подождать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to expect') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'equal' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: У меня на кухне все равны.
examples.trans: In my kitchen everyone is equal.

examples.text: У меня на кухне все равны!
examples.trans: In my kitchen everyone is equal!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'buddy', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Thank you for your kindness, buddy!
Your soup, buddy, enjoy your meal.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'critic, reviewer' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The restaurant critic praised the bartender.

examples.text: К нам сегодня приедет ресторанный критик.
examples.trans: A restaurant critic will come to us today.
A restaurant critic is sitting in the hall.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

рисковать.gloss: to risk, to take a risk

meanings.en: to risk, to take a risk
meanings.note: чем я рискую? = what have I got to lose?

examples.trans: What have I got to lose?
There's no need to take risks.

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'appetite', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('!') (= Enjoy your meal!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
+ infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Secondary conversational sense ('owe') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

уйти.gloss: to leave, to go away (on foot)

meanings.en: to leave, to go away, to walk out
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to leave, to go away (on foot)', paired with 'уходить'.
after a plural noun or pronoun: вы все
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (всем = to everyone (dative)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: И знаешь, что самое главное? Всем всё равно.
examples.trans: And you know the main thing? Nobody cares.

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.
